analysis: Examined the four files in this batch. (1) docs/reports/README.md: only a date bump and one new index link to a public-cluster-models record. It is documentation, with no security behavior. (2) ClusterConfiguration.swift (head lines 107-114, 169-174): the tensor-assistant validation is split into two require calls. The original conjunction still holds, including Qwen model/adapter, tensor-parallel mode, serial prefill and no private images. The `nativeMember == nil` check is now its own require with a new, more explanatory message (`tensorAssistantServesLocally`). The behavior is equivalent, so a coordinator-paired setup still cannot carry the unqualified speculative assistant, and the gate is not weakened. The change only affects the error text and the order of checks. Cross-file callers (`ClusterApprovalAttachment.attachment`, `ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection`) were not supplied; they are unchanged callers and not reviewed. (3) ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts+Release.swift (new): builds the release's cluster_runtime facts from bundled `ClusterPairServingGrants.records`, filtered by `isConsistent`, outcome == .passed and a stage adapter. It is a build-time/CLI helper that reads local candidate folders (config.json, manifest.json, catalog.json) from a directory the release tooling supplies. It fails closed when a qualified model cannot be described or when no models remain, and it only emits `note` messages for left-out entries. No network, secret or runtime authorization path is touched. Remaining unverified items: the implementations of `HashedInstallation.describe`, `facts`, `catalogArtifact` and `ClusterPairServingGrants` are outside the supplied evidence. I therefore cannot confirm that this file registers only the intended models, or that the coordinator's consumption of these facts is sound (TB-011, T-054). No concrete regression was identified.
